text:
alice: quick q — thinking about policy eval order: should we short-circuit region/compat checks before scoring (latency/cost) or score everything then filter? trying to avoid weird cross-region picks for latency wins
ben: +1 for filter-first. if a model isn't region-compatible we shouldn't waste score cycles on it. also avoids exposing cross-region options to tenants with region locks :lock:
carla: agree on filter-first for correctness, but watch out for capacity-based fallbacks. if region-filtered set is empty we need fallback scoring phase that considers tolerance thresholds
dinesh: yea fallback is key. my suggestion: 1) hard filters (region, tier, model-compat) 2) soft filters (latency/cost windows) 3) scoring with weight normalization. that lets us do preemptive fallback when hard-filter returns empty
eva: how do we encode soft filters in the policy DSL? can we express "prefer same-region up to +50ms" sort of thing?
frank: propose syntax like: ```policy { match tenant: "*" prefer_region: "same" soft_window_ms: 50 score { latency: 0.7 cost: 0.3 } }``` The engine applies soft_window as a penalty to off-region candidates
alice: that looks good. but we need to be explicit about metric direction (lower latency better, lower cost better) and normalization across units
ben: normalization idea: z-score with rolling baseline per model-region pair. convert latency and cost to unitless scores in [-1,1] then weighted sum. keeps weights stable across workloads
carla: rolling baseline is fine but we must bound influence: use clip and decay so a transient spike doesn't permanently shift scores
dinesh: operational concern: cache TTLs and route-compat cache invalidation. if we filter-first, cache keys should include region/tier constraints to avoid stale positives
eva: +1. also add policy-version into cache key. that way rollouts don't hit cached old decisions
route-bot: deploy check: policy-engine-v3 canary deployed to 10% of requests in eu-west-1 at 13:12 UTC — no errors reported in last 5m
frank: testing note: add synthetic harness that can flip capacity and region latency to validate fallback logic. keep tests as small fixtures not full e2e to iterate fast
alice: followups: (1) write RFC section on filter-first + fallback scoring (2) define DSL soft_window semantics (3) update cache key to include policy-version & region constraints (4) add canary tests in infra harness
carla: I'll start a draft for the RFC section, tag you all. planning to include a few sample policies and perf implications
dinesh: I'll open a PR to add policy-version to route cache key and add TTL bumping hooks
eva: I'll prototype the soft_window semantics in the policy-eval lib and share perf numbers
ben: once prototypes land we should run a 24h A/B on low-traffic tenants before full rollout :thumbsup:
alice: sweet — thanks team. evergreen todo: add health metrics for fallback rate and cross-region spills so SRE can alert if we regress
route-bot: note: canary traffic ramp to 25% scheduled at 14:00 UTC if no regressions observed
frank: :thinking_face: minor nit — document that scoring ties are resolved by least-recently-used penalty to avoid thrash
alice: noted, add tie-breaker LRU penalty to the RFC draft
carla: ok i'll include that and a short testing checklist. ping me on thread for reviews
frank: done reviewing draft section, left inline comments in PR
alice: closing loop — we'll sync on followups in architecture weekly to lock semantics before next sprint
